scope.statement: The CLI-first Hormuz alpha that authenticates Codex and Claude Code requests, enforces model, budget, DLP, and governed-context policy, relays OpenAI and Anthropic protocols, and records content-free control-plane evidence.
in_scope: HTTP ingress, authentication, policy, DLP, provider relay, and usage accounting
OIDC discovery, browser login, rotating SQLite or PostgreSQL sessions, and secure client credential custody
governed-context retrieval, lifecycle evidence, injection, and local persistence
configuration, build, CI, container, and release evidence boundaries
out_of_scope: provider-side systems beyond the documented HTTPS API contract
employee endpoints before requests enter Hormuz

a production PostgreSQL topology beyond the bounded accounting/identity/policy/session/approval slices, KMS, cache, reverse proxy, or multi-region deployment that has not been fully implemented or verified
an independent penetration test, which remains a separate release gate

assets.name: Provider API and billing administrator credentials
Employee, workload, and Hormuz session credentials
Organization model, budget, DLP, and context policy
Usage, token, cost, reservation, and billing metadata
Lifecycle evidence, snapshots, and verification state
Gateway availability and budget enforcement capacity
Tenant, actor, team, membership, and capability bindings

trust_boundaries.name: Provider egress
trust_boundaries.data: inspected provider requests, server-held provider credentials, streamed responses, and provider usage metadata

trust_boundaries.name: Identity provider

trust_boundaries.to: default SQLite usage/session/approval stores plus governed-context SQLite store

trust_boundaries.name: Lifecycle connector ingress
trust_boundaries.data: normalized evidence envelopes, repository snapshots, and revalidation requests

trust_boundaries.name: Build and release
trust_boundaries.to: Python distributions and private GHCR images

trust_boundaries.to: current PostgreSQL accounting/identity/policy/session/approval stores and future KMS, caches, queues, object storage, and observability systems

incident_scenarios.name: Identity provider outage or signing-key failure
Employee, provider, or signing credential compromise
Stale, poisoned, or contradictory context reaches a model
Unexpected token spend, budget bypass, or accounting drift
Customer export, deletion, residency, or legal-hold request

threats.title: Forged or replayed employee and workload identity
threats.scenario: An attacker presents a forged JWT, stolen bootstrap token, stale identity mapping, or replayed credential to act as another employee or workload.

controls.claim: Static tokens use constant-time comparison and OIDC JWTs require configured issuer, audience, algorithm, key, expiry, and subject mapping.
Authentication regression coverage includes malformed, expired, wrong-audience, wrong-issuer, unknown-key, and unmapped-subject denials.

threats.residual_risk: Bootstrap credentials remain available and real-IdP validation, SCIM, shared revocation, and hosted key custody are not complete.

threats.title: Cross-tenant data access through missing scope enforcement
threats.scenario: A missing application predicate, cache key, job binding, foreign key, or database policy exposes one tenant's data to another.

controls.claim: Current single-node APIs exercise identity-derived organization scope and cross-organization denials.
The accepted production contract requires mandatory tenant keys, application predicates, forced PostgreSQL RLS, and reused-connection isolation tests.
Schema-v4 migration and verification enforce separate roles, forced RLS, immutable tenant keys, read-only identity/policy projection privileges, exact columns, and transaction-local tenant context.

The digest-pinned two-tenant integration exercises migration idempotency, missing/cleared tenant context, reused-connection switching, cross-tenant denial, composite tenant foreign keys, accounting, desired-state identities and policies, multi-instance sessions, security evidence, and atomic one-time approvals.

threats.residual_risk: PostgreSQL is connected to accounting, human sessions, policy projections, DLP approvals, and security evidence, but governed context remains SQLite; pooled load, backup/restore, deletion, coordinated policy rollout, HA, KMS, SCIM, and independent review remain unproved.

threats.title: Provider credential exfiltration through upstream manipulation
threats.scenario: A caller or compromised upstream attempts to redirect a provider request or place credentials in an unsafe URL or forwarded header.

controls.claim: Provider base URLs are constrained, credentials are server-owned, redirects are refused, and caller headers are allowlisted and bounded.
Transport tests cover redirect refusal, fixed origin, unsafe URL rejection, and request metadata filtering.

threats.residual_risk: DNS, platform trust stores, egress firewalls, private endpoints, and provider-side systems remain deployment responsibilities.

threats.title: Sensitive content bypasses deterministic DLP
threats.scenario: Secrets, regulated identifiers, or company-specific values are hidden in unsupported encodings, media, archives, source paths, semantic paraphrases, or application-specific parsing.

controls.claim: The accepted deterministic-v2 subset covers credentials, selected regulated identifiers, bounded dictionaries, base64/percent/hex encoded text, queries, headers, and recognized opaque media.
Provider-aware DLP transformations, mixed-view precedence, encoded-text bounds, and fail-closed shapes have focused regression coverage.
Organization-specific evaluation remains explicit and content-free evidence is separated from the private corpus.

threats.residual_risk: Unknown encodings, archive contents, referenced files, semantic company information, and organization-specific quality thresholds remain open.

threats.title: Poisoned or stale governed context changes model behavior
threats.scenario: An obsolete, contradictory, or instruction-bearing record is retrieved and injected as trusted organizational knowledge.

controls.claim: Authorization, source/dependency freshness, bounded quarantine, contradiction handling, ranking, and token budgets precede rendering.
Retrieval tests cover scope, freshness, quarantine, contradictions, determinism, and budgeting.
The frozen release profile measures leakage, freshness, lifecycle, quality, and latency on a synthetic corpus.

threats.residual_risk: Detection is deterministic rather than semantic, source connectors are not automatic, customer data has not established quality, and continuation binding remains undecided.

threats.title: Forged lifecycle evidence promotes unverified memory
threats.scenario: An authenticated connector submits a syntactically valid but false merge, CI, review, ADR, incident, or human-confirmation event.

controls.claim: Evidence is immutable, subject-bound, versioned, conflict-aware, and promoter-gated.
The proposed first source collector separates signed GitHub App events from delegated workflow attestations.

threats.residual_risk: Authentication proves connector identity, not event truth; no owner-approved source protocol or signed collector is implemented.

threats.title: Session credential replay survives logout or authorization change
threats.scenario: A stolen refresh token, replayed family member, or stale identity mapping continues to authorize provider requests.

controls.claim: Opaque credentials are keyed-hash stored, rotate atomically, revoke on replay, and carry event-time tenant bindings.
PostgreSQL sessions route by a keyed opaque tenant tag, bind database authorization versions, and serialize refresh families transactionally across instances.
Two independent session repositories prove cross-instance enrollment/authentication, one-winner refresh rotation, replay-family revocation, and mapping-change invalidation.

threats.residual_risk: Shared immediate revocation is implemented for the bounded PostgreSQL path, but SCIM, real-IdP validation, KMS custody and rotation, pooling, backup/restore, and HA are not complete.

threats.title: Concurrent requests overspend organization or actor budgets
threats.scenario: Parallel requests observe stale totals or fail between reservation and settlement, allowing spend beyond configured caps.

controls.claim: SQLite reservations and settlements are atomic within the current single-node process.
Budget reservation, concurrency, release, and settlement behavior has deterministic regression coverage.

threats.residual_risk: No shared transaction or distributed admission contract exists across replicas.

threats.title: Provider usage or model metadata corrupts cost attribution
threats.scenario: Malformed, missing, duplicated, or attacker-controlled provider metadata creates false model, token, or cost records.

controls.claim: Provider metadata crosses explicit type, size, and allowlist boundaries and incomplete usage remains not available rather than zero-cost.
Accounting parsers cover malformed, incomplete, oversized, cached, reasoning, actual-model, and provider-native fields.
Provider aggregate facts stay separate from request estimates and person allocations are explicitly estimated.

threats.residual_risk: Scheduled provider polling, invoice and credit reconciliation, credential custody, and final finance workflows remain open.

threats.title: Audit evidence is altered, omitted, or deleted before export
threats.scenario: An operator or compromised process changes a SQLite or PostgreSQL ledger, deletes events, or replaces an audit export and its co-located anchor.

controls.claim: Canonical exports can carry a deterministic hash chain and validate against an externally retained count, head, and exact-file digest.
Mutation, truncation, reordering, wrong-anchor, and cross-store verification failures are tested.

threats.residual_risk: The chain is export-time evidence, not append-time signing, immutable storage, global sequencing, retention, legal hold, or KMS custody.

threats.title: Slow or oversized traffic exhausts gateway resources or spend
threats.scenario: Connections, headers, bodies, streams, or expensive requests consume threads, memory, provider capacity, or budgets faster than the process recovers.

controls.claim: The runtime bounds connections, parsed requests, headers, bodies, accounting buffers, upstream relay time, and graceful drain.
Real-socket tests cover saturation, slow headers and bodies, early EOF, oversized input, stream deadlines, recovery, and shutdown.

threats.residual_risk: Controls are process-local; no distributed throttling, source-aware WAF, replica coordination, or provider-quota failover exists.

threats.title: Provider or IdP outage cascades into unsafe availability behavior
threats.scenario: A dependency outage causes restart loops, unbounded waits, stale identity trust, or fail-open provider access.

controls.claim: OIDC metadata requests have bounded sizes, timeouts, caching, algorithm allowlists, and unknown-key refresh throttling.
Shallow probes avoid dependency-triggered restart loops and explicitly separate dependency monitoring from liveness.

threats.residual_risk: No production dependency SLO, deep-readiness policy, multi-provider failover policy, or tested incident runbook exists.

threats.title: Unauthorized configuration change weakens company policy
threats.scenario: A modified config reroutes models, raises budgets, disables DLP, changes identities, or rolls policy back without authorized review.

controls.claim: Configuration parsing is strict, reference-validated, immutable per process, and can bind exact file bytes to a deployment digest.
Unknown and duplicate fields, invalid references, unsafe URLs, digest mismatch, and immutable startup behavior are tested.

threats.residual_risk: A digest is not a signature; signer identity, approval authority, live rotation, and deployment-coordinated rollback remain absent.

threats.title: Compromised dependency or release workflow ships altered code
threats.scenario: Dependency drift, a mutable action, malicious build host, ref substitution, or unauthorized tag produces a release different from reviewed source.

controls.claim: CI pins actions and build inputs, verifies package/client closures, compares exact-source distributions and OCI layouts, and scans the restricted image.
Tag publication binds source, image digest, private package, keyless signature identity, SLSA provenance, and verification evidence.
Release triggers, repository, annotated tag, main reachability, image metadata, signing identity, and private package boundaries fail closed.

threats.residual_risk: Tag governance, protected reviewers, offline inputs, observed signed publication, KMS/offline signing, retention, and independent review remain open.

threats.title: Prompts, responses, credentials, or matched secrets enter telemetry
threats.scenario: Application logs, access logs, usage rows, error bodies, provider metadata, exports, or deployment components retain content or credentials.

controls.claim: Routine telemetry tables are bound to reviewed exact-column manifests and content-bearing fields are excluded.
Schema drift and prohibited telemetry columns fail closed.
The provider-content, usage, approval, context, log, and deployment-component boundaries are explicit.

threats.residual_risk: Reverse proxies, shippers, crash reporters, process dumps, providers, and the intentionally content-bearing context store require separate controls.

threats.title: Deletion, retention, legal hold, restore, or residency is incomplete
threats.scenario: A customer request is reported complete while data remains in a store, backup, replica, cache, export, or unapproved region, or required evidence is deleted.

controls.claim: The accepted decision requires a tenant data-class registry, isolated restore, auditable deletion, regional pinning, and legal-hold treatment.

threats.residual_risk: The accepted topology and schema foundation do not yet supply a durable-store registry, retention policy, backup/PITR, tenant restore, deletion workflow, or residency enforcement.

threats.title: Administrator or support access exceeds authorized scope
threats.scenario: A tenant administrator, Hormuz operator, support engineer, migration role, or compromised admin session reads content or changes policy outside a bounded approved capability.

controls.claim: Current local administrative APIs require explicit configured capabilities and derive organization from the authenticated identity.
The accepted decision separates tenant actors, runtime, owner, migration, operations, and time-bounded audited break-glass roles.

threats.residual_risk: Dynamic RBAC, support approval, break-glass, privileged-access management, role separation, and immutable admin audit are not implemented.

threats.title: Reusable cache leaks context across identities or survives invalidation
threats.scenario: A future context-pack cache omits tenant or authorization scope from its key, serves content after source or policy change, or conflicts with provider cache privacy policy.

controls.claim: The proposed cache boundary binds tenant, access scope, policy, source revisions, provider behavior, retention, and invalidation.

threats.residual_risk: Cache privacy tiers are unapproved and the reusable context-pack cache is intentionally not implemented.
